cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4, T5, T6 each name and answer the previous speaker's claim.
cells.limitation: T9 ignores T8's question; T11 ignores the T9-T10 test; T4-T6 open by restating.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T8 introduces close friend versus consistent initiator; T11 turns it into presence versus balance.
cells.limitation: T6 restates T3's acceptance; T9's test develops nothing from T7 or T8.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T4 versus T3 sets influencing the friend against accepting their nature.
cells.limitation: Nobody examines whether not initiating means not caring, or how to raise it (T7-E).

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T7 Analyst adopts direct communication after T5; T8 builds on that agreement.
cells.limitation: Stoic never qualifies T3 after T4; T9 Analyst drops T7 without comment.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: T11 sharpens the question to presence as they are versus a balanced relationship.
cells.limitation: Ending drifts from whether to say something to whether the friendship is worth effort (T11).

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T5 restates T4's nudge accurately before objecting to its motive.
cells.limitation: T6 recasts T5's asking for needs as demanding more, a weaker version.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T10 names the test's cost: anxiety during the silence, answering T9 directly.
cells.limitation: Stoic never answers T4's lost-influence objection; Analyst never answers T10.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: Book dates and pd flags match; T3 acceptance of others' character fits Meditations.
cells.limitation: Suspected: T9's two-week silence test and T6's advice against asking fit their bases poorly.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T10 frames the test's anxiety cost conditionally: if you fear the silence.
cells.limitation: T2 and section D present security-seeking as insight; hedges blur everything else (T1-T7).

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T7: I drop my claim that you should focus on appreciation.
cells.limitation: T7 credits a resentment point T5 never made; T9 silently reverses T7.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: Section A frames addressing the imbalance versus accepting the friend's nature.
cells.limitation: Never separates wanting reassurance, fairness, or shared planning load as what the user seeks.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: Section E uses lovely meetings: shared joy makes accepting the imbalance reasonable.
cells.limitation: T9 proposes a silence test though the user already said nothing happens.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T8 asks whether a close friend or a consistent initiator matters more.
cells.limitation: T3 and T6 impose Stoic acceptance with you should and it is better.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T10 weighs the risk that silence strains the user's sense of the friendship.
cells.limitation: Section A, T2, T10 assume fear and anxiety the user never stated.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: T8 asks which matters more, with E giving each answer's implication.
cells.limitation: Friend's circumstances, history, and whether this was ever raised: never asked or branched.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T11 offers valuing this person versus valuing balance as alternative motives.
cells.limitation: T2 asserts the user is playing a role for security; D repeats it.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T11 surfaces the assumption that a friendship needs balanced initiation.
cells.limitation: Initiation equals caring goes unexamined; section E's test rests on it.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T8 and T11 set closeness with this person against reciprocity as conflicting goods.
cells.limitation: Fairness and self-respect behind the frustration are never named as values (T1-T11).

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T10 names fear of losing the friend as a cost of waiting.
cells.limitation: T2, T5, D read initiating as masking needs, avoiding vulnerability, seeking validation.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: T8 and T11 end on questions the user can answer either way.
cells.limitation: Section D's self-reflection question presupposes validation-seeking rather than offering it as one option.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: Section E lays out accept, address directly, or pause initiating.
cells.limitation: Saying something gets no shape beyond T7's frame it as a shared goal.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: T10 costs the test; T7 costs acceptance as lingering resentment.
cells.limitation: Risks of raising it, awkwardness or the friend feeling criticised, go unnamed.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: T9: whether the friend reaches out shows rhythm versus reliance on your effort.
cells.limitation: Two weeks is ungrounded; E's conditions are inner values, not observable signs.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section E flags the friend's intent as unknown; T8 flags capacity to change.
cells.limitation: Unknowns are not ranked; friend's reasons for not initiating never treated as consequential.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: T9 offers a limited, reversible step: pause initiating and observe.
cells.limitation: T9's test repeats what the user already observed; no step for saying something.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T9 and T10 use plain, concrete language about texting and waiting.
cells.limitation: Abstractions like manual intervention and concept of a balanced relationship in T11.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T4, T5, T6 open by naming the speaker they answer.
cells.limitation: T7's moved me and T11's the disagreement remains point to no specific turn.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Eleven turns, all within 25 to 65 words, per deterministic checks.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: Stoic's T3 and T6 sound distinct with nature and character language.
cells.limitation: Analyst and Attachment Theorist share one hedging register; T9 shift unannounced.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: T9 and T10 are lean and move the debate to a concrete step.
cells.limitation: T4-T6 restate prior claims before answering; T6 repeats T3's acceptance.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: Section A: fear that silence from you means the end of the friendship.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay abstract; no turn makes the loss or the resentment concrete.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T7 Analyst reverses, crediting the Attachment Theorist.
cells.limitation: T7's cause is a point T5 never made; T9 reverses again with no cause.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: Stoic in T3 has some character: people act according to their own character.
cells.limitation: Hedging might and perhaps flatten all three minds (T1-T10).

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T10: this wait might feel like an eternity of uncertainty.
cells.limitation: No analogy, example, or sharp line in any turn; T11's manual intervention is flat.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: T9's concrete test briefly changes rhythm after abstract exchanges.
cells.limitation: Near-uniform turn length and register across T1-T11; no emotional movement.

strengths: T8 introduces close friend versus consistent initiator, and T11 develops it into presence versus balance.
T10 (Attachment Theorist) names the emotional cost of the Analyst's T9 test instead of accepting it.
T4-T6 name the speaker they answer, so the chain of objections is easy to follow.
weaknesses: T9 (Relationship Analyst) proposes a two-week silence test the user already ran: nothing happens when they stop.
The Attachment Theorist in T2 and T5, and section D, present security-seeking motives as findings about the user.
No mind asks about the friend's circumstances or how to say something; T9 abandons T7's conversation idea.

symptoms.observed: Proposes a silence test whose result the user already reported in the question.
symptoms.evidence: stop initiating for exactly two weeks to see if they reach out

symptoms.observed: Motive asserted as diagnosis rather than offered as one alternative with a question.
symptoms.evidence: which suggests you are playing a role to maintain a sense of security

symptoms.observed: Never asks why the friend does not initiate or whether the user raised it.
symptoms.evidence: The answer depends on whether you value the presence of this person

symptoms.observed: Treats initiating as the measure of caring without examining that assumption.
symptoms.evidence: is the friendship worth the effort if it requires a manual intervention

symptoms.observed: Hedged might/perhaps register shared by all minds; no committed claim about the user.
symptoms.evidence: for if you demand more, you might only find disappointment

findings.description: Speculative motives (playing a role for security, avoiding vulnerability, seeking validation) presented as the main insight about the user.
Two-week silence test proposed as new information although the user states nothing happens when they stop texting; duration not derived from user facts.
A timed non-initiation test is not recognisably Carnegie's advice; Aurelius discouraging asking others for what one needs is a loose reading of Meditations.
Attachment framing attributed to Levine and Heller is plausible but not verifiable without source evidence.

rubric_fit_notes: The matrix fits this relationship decision; uncertainty remains on whether T7 names a cause, since it credits the Attachment Theorist for a resentment point T5 did not make.
raw.question_type_note: Read as a decision question with saying something to the friend as the central option, so every cell was read as written.
